# SB-1006 — Safety bulletin: hot metal and scale ejection

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Hazard description
Hot metal and scale ejection from furnace operations present impact and burn hazards to operators and bystanders, and can damage tooling, conveyors, and nearby equipment. Ejection events are most commonly observed during loading, quench entry, and quench immersion when scale fractures or molten droplets are dislodged. Contributing factors include improper containment, delayed quench entry, degraded hearth or basket condition, and failure of local shielding. The immediate risks are thermal injury, eye damage, slip hazards from quench splash, and secondary projectiles from broken scale.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) on P1-L4 and all associated quench staging and shielding fixtures used with this furnace. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds. Related process staging areas and any manual handling stations adjacent to the furnace are included. See ECN-2026-015 for recent configuration changes, and SOP-P1-L4-03 and SOP-P1-L4-05 for operating and maintenance procedures referenced below.

Required controls
- Engineering: Verify fixed shields, splash guards, and quench entry baffles are installed per ECN-2026-015 and are free of deformation or gaps before each shift. Restrict pedestrian access to the minimum required area and install permanent signage at the exclusion boundary.  
- Administrative: Enforce adherence to SOP-P1-L4-03 and SOP-P1-L4-05 for loading, quench timing, and basket inspection. Do not exceed the specified quench delay; operators must time entry so that delay does not exceed the stated maximum. Record quench timing on the heat sheet for every cycle.  
- PPE: Require face shields, heat-resistant gloves, and arm protection for all personnel within the exclusion boundary during loading and quench operations. Provide splash mats at quench exits to mitigate slip.  
- Inspection: Implement daily visual checks of shielding and quarterly documented inspections of quench hardware; remove from service and tag out any component exhibiting cracks, excessive wear, or deformation.

Effective date
Effective date: Upon release.
